$comment: What npm run design-check renders and measures. On each theme it renders every pattern in patterns/ once per section style, with one link put into the body text of link.pattern, and loads the page at each width: contrast measures every element holding text against its background, at rest and, for links and buttons, hovered; overflow and motion are measured per section, motion with reduced motion emulated and two samples motion.gap_ms apart. motion.moves_with_motion_on names the patterns that animate when motion is on, so the run checks it can see them move. wp is the WordPress version the theme runs on: Twenty Twenty-Five and Twenty Twenty-Four on the stable release that bundles them, and Ipsum, WordPress's proposed default theme, which requires 7.2, on the 7.2 beta. install pins a theme that is not bundled with WordPress or on WordPress.org to a commit, installed from GitHub's archive of it, so a moving trunk never changes the run. roles is the role map get-catalog must report on that theme: a positive control that the map under test is the one in use. plant is the low-contrast role map the contrast control sets through voyager_open_blocks_style_roles; the control passes only when every target at rest in the planted style fails (a hover can be the theme's own, such as Twenty Twenty-Four's grey outline hover). On ipsum, which has no built-in map, the plant changes on-accent alone, so the Accent background the control measures is still the fallback's. controls sets the width each planted control loads at, and how wide the overflow plant's element is. variations lists the colour-bearing style variations the theme ships; each is switched on as the Site Editor saves one and measured for contrast only, at variations.widths. known_failures lists the pairs measured under the floor, with the ratio measured, and an empty variation is the theme's own styles: the run passes them, fails on every other pair under the floor, and fails when a listed pair no longer fails.

link.text: we will get back to you

a11y.$comment: a11y runs axe-core on every section render: the rules tagged with these WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 A and AA tags, plus rules, which names heading-order because axe tags it best-practice. The context is the sections, so the theme's own markup cannot fail the pack, and page-level rules do not run. Any violation fails the render; incomplete results are printed as advisories.

impeccable.$comment: impeccable runs impeccable detect --json --no-config on the page at each width and places each finding in the section its selector matches. gate is the Impeccable 4.8.2 rule ids (impeccable detect --list-rules) a finding in a section fails on; every other finding, and a gated one in the theme's own markup, is printed as an advisory. Impeccable 4.8.2 has no tap-target rule, so the check measures tap targets itself: every link, button and form control in a section must be tap_target.min px tall and wide, apart from a link in a run of text. known_gaps lists, per theme, a kind of target the theme draws under the minimum and the height measured; a target of that kind within tolerance px of it passes, and a listed gap that is no longer measured fails.
